title: Kathak tatkar footwork rhythm
summary: Tatkar is the footwork of kathak, the classical dance of northern India: bare feet strike the floor in exact patterns of speed and precision while strings of small brass bells (ghungroo) round the ankles mark every footfall. The dancer speaks the same pattern aloud in syllables as she dances.
howToPlay: Four movements are lit beside the dancer: Ta is the right foot, Thei the left foot, Tat a quick pair of heel taps, and Dha a spring on both feet with the arms thrown wide.
A ring closes on a movement when it is due. Tap it as the ring closes and the dancer answers; listen to the bells ring on every step.
Begin with the sixteen-beat cycle, then try the quick tatkar at twice the speed.
rules: A tap right on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and taps with no ring open cost points.
Each pattern is played twice through; the long pattern is counted in sixteen beats.
Patterns are simplified teaching figures in the style of the dance, not choreography to copy.
heritageNote: Kathak is traced to the wandering storytellers of northern India and was refined at the royal courts; it is now taught and performed in India, Pakistan and around the world. Tatkar is the first footwork every student learns.
